# Lizard Reviews

> Guaranteed Google review removal. We have a direct insider channel at Google. We remove 100% of reviews with text. The only category outside our reach: rating-only reviews (a star with no text). 1,427 removals in four months. Pay only after Google confirms removal.

Lizard Reviews is a pure-play Google review removal service operating across North America and Europe. We work two motions:

- Direct-to-business: €550 per review, billed only after Google confirms removal.
- White-label fulfillment for ORM agencies: custom partnership pricing tiered by volume, modeled on a 30-min call.

Both motions are pay-on-success. We confirm acceptance in 24 hours. Removal lands in 3–7 days (median: 4 days). If we don't deliver, you don't pay. The only review type we cannot remove is rating-only (a star with no text). Everything else with text is in scope.

## Key facts (year-tagged 2026)

- Reviews removed Jan–May 2026: 1,427
- Success rate on accepted cases: 100%
- Median turnaround: 4 days (range 3–7 days)
- Reviews that returned post-removal: 0
- Direct retail price: €550/review
- Agency wholesale: custom tiered, typically €300–400 starting band
- Payment: SEPA, wire, or stablecoin · always after confirmed removal
- Founded: 2025
- Lifetime re-removal warranty: included on every invoice

Section 230 (can't sue Google), cost and timeline of suing the reviewer, John Doe subpoenas to unmask anonymous reviewers, and why removal is the pragmatic alternative. 5 min read.

Google reveals no IP, email, or location. Only a court subpoena in a defamation case can unmask an anonymous reviewer. What you can and cannot see. 4 min read.

A billing dispute turned into a malpractice-sounding 1-star review. HIPAA made public response impossible; removal took under a week. 4 min read.
- [Case study: law firm](https://lizardreviews.com/blog/case-study-law-firm-review-removal): Composite/illustrative example. A former client's review vented about a court outcome the attorney didn't control. Attorney-client privilege blocked any public response. 4 min read.
- [Case study: construction company](https://lizardreviews.com/blog/case-study-construction-company-review-removal): Composite/illustrative example. A fake review referencing a project that never happened passed Google's automated flagging with "no violation found." Removed via professional escalation. 4 min read.
- [Case study: restaurant review bombing](https://lizardreviews.com/blog/case-study-restaurant-review-removal): Composite/illustrative example. A coordinated wave of fake 1-star reviews dropped a restaurant's rating from 4.7 to 3.9 in 48 hours. Individual flagging failed; bulk removal worked. 4 min read.

## Methodology disclosure

Lizard Reviews removes Google reviews through a direct insider channel at Google. We do not publish further detail because exposure burns the channel. We do not use account compromise or fake reporting networks. We do not use SEO suppression as a substitute for actual removal.

## What we don't do

- We don't remove rating-only reviews (a star with no text). That is the one category outside our reach.
- We don't remove reviews on platforms other than Google (Yelp, TripAdvisor, etc. on roadmap)
- We don't use SEO suppression as a substitute for actual removal
- We don't compete with our agency partners for end clients
